title: Regional capacity handshake and drain coordination for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a deterministic handshake and coordinated draining protocol between regional dedicated fleets and fallback/shared pools to guarantee committed throughput while respecting data residency constraints. This ticket covers the control-plane protocol, safe drain windows, pre-warm allocation steps, and observability hooks required to move customer traffic gracefully across zones/regions when capacity changes or outages occur.
context: Customers on Dedicated plans require both throughput guarantees and strict residency bounds. Today, abrupt zone evacuations or scaling events can cause noisy neighbor impact or accidental cross-region processing when we naively spill traffic to hosted/shared pools. We need a predictable, auditable handoff that: (1) preserves per-customer residency constraints, (2) meets committed throughput targets during transitions, and (3) minimizes total token loss and request latency spikes.
proposed_solution: Introduce a regional 'capacity handshake' protocol between the Dedicated orchestrator and fallback targets. Key elements: 1) capacity reservation intent messages that include customer residency flags and throughput floor/ceiling, 2) staged drain windows (prepare -> hold -> cutover) with configurable grace periods, 3) pre-warm allocation calls to target pools with KV cache warm-up hints, 4) rate-limited transfer of live connections and a token-level accounting snapshot to minimize double-billing or lost tokens, and 5) policy enforcement to block cross-region spill if residency prohibits it, with fallback to same-region hosted variants or queued requests. The control-plane exposes audit events and decision traces for SRE/Customer Success.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dedicated orchestrator can initiate a handshake and receive deterministic ACK/NACK from fallback targets within existing control-plane APIs. 2) During a simulated zone drain (chaos test), no customer with a region-only residency setting is served outside their region. 3) Throughput for committed dedicated contracts remains within 95% of floor during the hold phase for >= 1 minute (configurable). 4) KV cache warm-up reduces median token-generation latency by >= 20% in first 30s after cutover vs naive cold start. 5) Audit trail contains time-stamped decision events and token accounting snapshots for each handoff. 6) New metrics (transfer_latency, handoff_success_rate, residency_violation_count) visible in Console and used by alerts.
implementation_steps: Design control-plane handshake proto: fields = customer_id, residency_policy, throughput_floor, throughput_ceiling, preferred_fallbacks, warmup_hints, correlation_id
Extend orchestrator: initiate handshake, transition state machine (PREPARE -> HOLD -> CUTOVER -> VERIFY -> COMPLETE/ROLLBACK)
Implement fallback adapters: accept reservation intent, execute pre-warm sequence (model weights + KV hints), respond with capacity_estimate and accept_window
Enforce residency policies in routing layer: add deny-list for cross-region spill; implement queued-batch fallback when no same-region capacity exists
Add token-level snapshot API: emit per-request tokens-start/tokens-complete markers to avoid misaccounting during transfer
Expose events to Console: handoff_start, warmup_ready, cutover_initiated, cutover_complete, handoff_rolled_back
Create chaos test harness: scripted zone drain simulating host reboots and scale-downs across regions
Add unit/integration tests and run end-to-end scenarios with sample dedicated customer config
Document operator runbook and update runbooks for Customer Success for manual interventions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): local e2e with 2-region simulator and sample customers (feature-flagged)
Phase 1 (staging): enable for internal teams and opt-in customers; run 72h soak and chaos drains nightly
Phase 2 (limited prod): enable for a subset of Dedicated fleets with low criticality; monitor metrics and SLOs for 1 week
Phase 3 (general): flip default for all regional Dedicated fleets; deprecate legacy spillover behavior after two-week observation window
rollback_plan: If handoff_failure_rate > 2% or residency_violation_count > 0 in the first 24 hours after a rollout step, automatically pause new handoffs and revert to legacy safe-queue behavior while routing engineers investigate. Maintain a manual escalation path for affected customers to request immediate reversion to pinned-region routing.
metrics: handoff_success_rate: percentage of successful handshake->complete transitions
transfer_latency_ms: median/90/99 of time between handoff_start and cutover_complete
residency_violation_count: count of requests processed outside allowed region
throughput_retained_pct: percent of committed throughput maintained during HOLD phase
kv_warmup_latency_reduction: delta in median token latency post-warmup vs cold
risks: Pre-warm spikes could temporarily increase GPU memory usage if we over-provision warmup; need conservative warmup sizing
Complexity in token accounting may create billing edge cases — require audit and PR review with Billing team
If fallback targets NACK due to capacity, customers could experience queued delays; must surface clear retry windows
Cross-region network partitions could leave orchestrator in uncertain state — add leader election/timeouts
open_questions: What is the acceptable minimum hold duration for enterprise SLAs? (PM to confirm)
Should pre-warm warmup_hints include per-customer KV prefixes or only model-level state?
Do we allow a best-effort cross-region spill for non-residency customers as an emergency escape hatch?
Who owns billing edge-case investigations when partial tokens are credited across two pools?
